title: The Silent Strings Case
story:
In the dimly lit jazz club 'Whispers & Rhythms', the evening took a sinister turn. The enigmatic pianist, Mr. Ezra Blackwood, was found dead behind the piano, his life extinguished by a single gunshot wound.

Victim: Mr. Ezra Blackwood (enigmatic pianist)
Crime Scene: Whispers & Rhythms Jazz Club
Forensic Clue: A faint whispering sound heard at the time of murder.

Testimonies:
1. The bartender, Miss Amelia Sparks: "I heard a peculiar sound around the time of the murder, similar to 'Whispers & Rhythms' name."
2. Dancing couple, Mr. and Mrs. Charles Evans: "We noticed a strange, rhythmic noise while indulging in our dance."
3. Private investigator, Mr. Julian Drake: "I arrived shortly after the murder and heard a peculiar noise, too."
4. Bandleader, Mr. Theo Knight: "The club was busy, I didn't pay much heed to any noise."


Question: Who is the silent assassin and how did they commit the crime?
Options:
0. Miss Amelia Sparks (heard a whispering sound)
1. Mr. Julian Drake (arrived shortly after the crime and heard a noise)
2. Mr. Theo Knight (heard a noise but didn't pay attention)
3. Mr. Charles Evans (heard a noise during their dance)
4. Mrs. Charles Evans (heard a noise during their dance)


Correct Index: 1 (Mr. Julian Drake arrived shortly after the crime and heard a noise)


Deduction Explanation: The forensic clue of a faint whispering sound being heard at the time of murder leads to suspect 1 (Miss Amelia Sparks), suspect 3 (Mr. Charles Evans), suspect 4 (Mrs. Charles Evans), and suspect 2 (Mr. Theo Knight). However, suspect 1 and 4 only heard the noise after the crime happened, while suspects 3 and 2 didn't pay attention to the noise. Only suspect 1 (Miss Amelia Sparks) has the motive - she had a grudge against Mr. Blackwood due to a previous altercation. Suspect 1's testimony is the only one that matches the time frame of the crime.

Therefore, the person who arrives shortly after the crime, suspect 1 (Mr. Julian Drake), is the most likely culprit as they have a motive and heard the noise at the correct time.

The mysterious 'Whispers & Rhythms Jazz Club' was filled with a lively crowd, celebrating the memorable performance by Mr. Ezra Blackwood. The piano artist, Mr. Ezra Blackwood, seemed to be enjoying his performance when a violent outburst broke out from the backstage. Curiously, the quarrel ended abruptly with Mr. Blackwood's murder. All witnesses heard a noise around the time of the crime - a faint whispering sound.

The next morning, detectives discover a mysterious note left behind at the crime scene. The note reads: 'No more whispers, Ezra.' A cryptic message that hints towards a hidden motive.

The town's gossip queen, Miss Amelia Sparks, had a heated argument with Mr. Blackwood a week ago, over the club's financial management. Suspect 1, Mr. Julian Drake, arrived shortly after the crime occurred. Notably, the club was abuzz with noise, yet nobody else heard the mysterious whispering sound so distinctly as Miss Amelia Sparks did.
